examination: Civil Services Mains Examination - Optional Subject
document_type: Official Syllabus, Sociology Paper I (Fundamentals of Sociology)
provenance_note: Unit and clause text is the published UPSC syllabus for Sociology Paper I, corroborated across independent reproductions including one claiming clause-by-clause reproduction from the CSE 2026 notification. NOT diffed against the notification PDF itself. Verify before promoting any mention to verified.
structure_note: Paper I has ten numbered units and no lettered parts - unlike PSIR, whose paper sections map to named syllabus parts. The units are the topic level; their (a)/(b)/(c) clauses are the microtopics. section_ref is omitted because the syllabus makes no such division; the question paper's Section A/B cut is a property of the paper, not the syllabus (rev2 M10).
paper_title_note: paper_title MUST equal subjects.name for slug upsc-cse-mains-opt-sociology-p1 exactly, or resolve_subject creates a duplicate.

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Sociology - The Discipline: (a) Modernity and social changes in Europe and emergence of sociology. (b) Scope of the subject and comparison with other social sciences. (c) Sociology and common sense.
micro_themes: Modernity and social changes in Europe and the emergence of sociology
Scope of the subject and comparison with other social sciences

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Sociology as Science: (a) Science, scientific method and critique. (b) Major theoretical strands of research methodology. (c) Positivism and its critique. (d) Fact value and objectivity. (e) Non-positivist methodologies.
micro_themes: Major theoretical strands of research methodology

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Research Methods and Analysis: (a) Qualitative and quantitative methods. (b) Techniques of data collection. (c) Variables, sampling, hypothesis, reliability and validity.
micro_themes: Variables, sampling, hypothesis, reliability and validity

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Sociological Thinkers: (a) Karl Marx - Historical materialism, mode of production, alienation, class struggle. (b) Emile Durkheim - Division of labour, social fact, suicide, religion and society. (c) Max Weber - Social action, ideal types, authority, bureaucracy, protestant ethic and the spirit of capitalism. (d) Talcott Parsons - Social system, pattern variables. (e) Robert K. Merton - Latent and manifest functions, conformity and deviance, reference groups. (f) Mead - Self and identity.
micro_themes: Karl Marx: historical materialism, mode of production, alienation, class struggle
Emile Durkheim: division of labour, social fact, suicide, religion and society
Max Weber: social action, ideal types, authority, bureaucracy, protestant ethic and the spirit of capitalism
Talcott Parsons: social system, pattern variables
Robert K. Merton: latent and manifest functions, conformity and deviance, reference groups
G. H. Mead: self and identity

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Stratification and Mobility: (a) Concepts - equality, inequality, hierarchy, exclusion, poverty and deprivation. (b) Theories of social stratification - Structural functionalist theory, Marxist theory, Weberian theory. (c) Dimensions - Social stratification of class, status groups, gender, ethnicity and race. (d) Social mobility - open and closed systems, types of mobility, sources and causes of mobility.
micro_themes: Concepts: equality, inequality, hierarchy, exclusion, poverty and deprivation
Dimensions: stratification by class, status group, gender, ethnicity and race
Social mobility: open and closed systems, types, sources and causes

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Works and Economic Life: (a) Social organization of work in different types of society - slave society, feudal society, industrial/capitalist society. (b) Formal and informal organization of work. (c) Labour and society.
micro_themes: Social organization of work in slave, feudal and industrial/capitalist society
Formal and informal organization of work

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Politics and Society: (a) Sociological theories of power. (b) Power elite, bureaucracy, pressure groups and political parties. (c) Nation, state, citizenship, democracy, civil society, ideology. (d) Protest, agitation, social movements, collective action, revolution.
micro_themes: Power elite, bureaucracy, pressure groups and political parties
Nation, state, citizenship, democracy, civil society, ideology
Protest, agitation, social movements, collective action, revolution

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Religion and Society: (a) Sociological theories of religion. (b) Types of religious practices: animism, monism, pluralism, sects, cults. (c) Religion in modern society: religion and science, secularization, religious revivalism, fundamentalism.
micro_themes: Types of religious practices: animism, monism, pluralism, sects, cults
Religion in modern society: religion and science, secularization, religious revivalism, fundamentalism

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Systems of Kinship: (a) Family, household, marriage. (b) Types and forms of family. (c) Lineage and descent. (d) Patriarchy and sexual division of labour. (e) Contemporary trends.
micro_themes: Patriarchy and sexual division of labour

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Social Change in Modern Society: (a) Sociological theories of social change. (b) Development and dependency. (c) Agents of social change. (d) Education and social change. (e) Science, technology and social change.
